subject: RFI: Security architecture & isolation model — detailed responses and diagrams
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-tech.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: RFP request — security architecture artifacts (network diagrams, threat model)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of Acme's security review we need a few items to proceed:

- A VPC/network diagram showing isolation between tenant workloads for Hosted and Private deployments.
- A short (1–2 page) threat model summary and mitigations for data exfil and privileged key compromise.
- Details on KMS integration, key rotation, and separation of customer keys for Private deployments.
- Evidence of audit logging (what's captured, retention) and where logs are stored.

Can you provide these artifacts and an initial set of answers to our security questionnaire? Procurement needs those to move to an ITO review. We are aiming to complete the security gating by the 20th of Feb.

I've attached our security questionnaire (ACME_Security_Q_2026.docx) as a baseline. If you prefer, we can schedule a 60-minute architecture Q&A later this week.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and ETA.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Security Engineer, Acme Tech
security-phx@acme-tech.com

Attachment: ACME_Security_Q_2026.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-tech.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-tech.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP request — security architecture artifacts (network diagrams, threat model)

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything on your checklist. Initial plan and ETA below: 

Deliverables (ETA 48 hours):
- Redwood network diagram (Hosted, Dedicated, Private VPC variants) — redwood_network_diagram_v2.png
- Threat model summary (1.5 pages) — redwood_threat_model_summary.pdf
- Completed question set (your doc: ACME_Security_Q_2026) — acme_security_questionnaire_filled.docx
- RFI spreadsheet with per-question answers and evidentiary links — rfi_answers_sheet.xlsx

High-level notes up front:
- Isolation model: Hosted deployments use tenant-level logical isolation inside multi-tenant runtime with per-request encryption-in-transit and per-tenant metadata separation. Private (VPC) deployments give network-level isolation with customer-managed subnets and optional private peering.
- Key management: We integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) for Private. Hosted can use customer-managed keys via our BYOK flow and envelope encryption; we rotate service keys quarterly and support customer-triggered rotation for BYOK.
- Audit logs: All API activity, admin actions, model load events, and key access attempts are logged. Logs are stored in immutable write-once S3 buckets (or equivalent in-customer project for Private) with configurable retention; default retention 90 days for hosted; enterprise plans and Private can configure longer retention.

I'll attach the artifacts to this thread; Rafael will add a brief section on our runtime threat mitigations (KV cache isolation, replay protections). If you're OK, we'd like to schedule a 60-minute architecture review on Fri 13th or Mon 16th.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: redwood_network_diagram_v2.png (image/png), redwood_threat_model_summary.pdf (application/pdf), rfi_answers_sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme-tech.com, security-phx@acme-tech.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP request — security architecture artifacts (network diagrams, threat model)

Marissa —

Received the initial package, thanks. A few quick clarifying questions from our infra and crypto teams after a first pass:

1) For Hosted: Can you confirm whether tenant traffic ever crosses customer boundaries at the TCP level (i.e., shared L3/L4) or whether every inference request is handled in contained containers/processes with enforced network fences?

2) KMS/BYOK: For the BYOK flow, does Redwood ever have access to plaintext customer keys or unwrapped customer root keys? What is the sequence for wrapping/unwrapping during key provisioning?

3) KV cache isolation: In the threat model you mention KV cache partitioning — is that enforced in-memory, or do you persist shared caches to disk? What controls prevent cross-tenant cache snooping?

4) Audit evidence: We need an example audit record format (redacted) showing model load, request origin, token count, and KMS key id usage. Can you paste a sample JSON log entry?

5) Private deployment networking: If we run Private in our AWS account, can we enforce that control plane calls (e.g., telemetry, license checks) are blocked and that only call-home allowed flows are via customer-controlled egress through a firewall?

If you can answer inline and include short samples where possible that will speed our review.

Regards,
Liam

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-tech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-tech.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP request — security architecture artifacts (network diagrams, threat model)

Hi Liam —

Appended below are short, concrete answers to your inline questions plus an anonymized sample log. We also uploaded the full artifacts and a diagram set to the shared folder (link below). If helpful, we can redact and produce a one-page hardcopy SOC2 evidence bundle for your ITO.

1) Hosted network boundaries
- Tenant traffic: runtime operates on multi-tenant GPU pools. Network-level flow is shared at L3/L4 in our host VPCs (cloud provider fabric), but application-level isolation is enforced by sandboxed runtime processes and strong mutual authentication between the front-door (API gateway) and worker nodes. Each request is scoped to a tenant context; inter-tenant network reachability is blocked by host firewall rules and service mesh policies. In short: shared L3/L4 fabric, enforced isolation at process and firewall level to prevent lateral movement.

2) BYOK key handling
- Sequence: customer imports public-wrapped key metadata to Redwood -> Redwood creates a wrapping key in our HSM -> customer wraps their DEK (data encryption key) using the wrapping key and provides the wrapped DEK to Redwood -> Redwood stores only wrapped DEKs; unwrapped keys are never stored. 
- Access: Redwood does not store plaintext customer root keys. For Hosted BYOK, an ephemeral unwrapping step occurs in an HSM-protected boundary during provisioning; audit events record the unwrapping operation.

3) KV cache isolation
- Implementation: KV caches are partitioned per-tenant in memory. We avoid persisting shared cache shards to disk for Hosted. If a policy requires persistence (Private/dedicated), persisted caches are written to customer-owned volumes or encrypted tenant-specific stores. Access control checks and per-tenant memory tagging mitigate cross-tenant snooping.

4) Sample audit record (redacted)
- Example JSON:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-12T21:10:03Z",
  "event": "model_load",
  "tenant_id": "redwood-acme-01",
  "request_id": "req-4f7a23b1",
  "model": "gpt-small-alpha-v1",
  "token_count": 128,
  "source_ip": "198.51.100.23",
  "kms_key_id": "projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/rdw-key-01"
}

(We can provide a signed, redacted sample on request.)

5) Private deployment control-plane calls
- Yes. Private deployments can be deployed with a control-plane-egress-block policy. In that mode, the local control plane makes no external calls by default; telemetry and license checks are disabled or routed via customer-controlled egress (e.g., an outbound proxy or a collected telemetry aggregator). We provide a call-home sandbox if you want periodic license heartbeats — that can be restricted to a single IP range and port and requires mutual TLS.

Next steps: I've attached the final RFI sheet and a concise PDF threat model summary. Marissa, Vivek and I are available for the architecture review. Please propose two times and we'll lock one.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_threat_model_summary.pdf, rfi_answers_sheet.xlsx
